title: Desktop Companion
subtitle: Your desktop companion is quietly learning to understand you better. All data stays local and collection is fully opt-in.

secrets.title: Browser credentials
secrets.hint: Stored credentials are shared by your browser sessions and can be injected by reference. The value is encrypted on this machine and never shown again or sent to the model — only injected when the page's domain matches the allowed origins. The allowed origins also limit which domains the browser may send data to.
secrets.valueWriteOnly: Write-only: encrypted on this device, never shown again or sent to the model.
secrets.originsHint: One per line or comma-separated. Reduced to registrable domains. The credential is only injected on these domains, which also become the browser's egress allowlist.
secrets.originsRequired: At least one allowed origin is required.

memories.mergeHint: For each group, pick the entries to merge, edit the merged text, then confirm. Merged sources are archived (never deleted).

collect.clearConfirm: This deletes everything under companion/flowy/events. Learned memories are unaffected. Continue?
collect.clearHint: Deletes raw event files only; learned memories stay.
collect.disableAllConfirm: Stop all collection, learning and evolution? Learned skills and memories are kept, model config is unchanged, and you can re-enable anytime.

sources.desc: Turning one off stops new records of that kind; the ones already kept still feed learning until the retention policy below removes them. These switches belong to this device — every companion learns from the same records.

tool_calls.desc: Which tools were called in work sessions: only the tool name and the param shape (top-level arg names and types) — never arg values, never results.

chat_user_messages.name: Chat prompts
chat_user_messages.desc: The verbatim questions you send in conversations (very long ones are truncated).

requirements.desc: Titles, descriptions and tags of requirements you create.

terminal_sessions.name: Terminal session metadata
terminal_sessions.desc: Terminal create/exit records — no commands and no output content.

companion_dialogues.name: Messages to companions
companion_dialogues.desc: The verbatim things you say to a desktop companion (long ones are truncated). The companion’s own replies are not recorded; replies stored by earlier versions still take up space but no longer feed learning, and the retention policy cleans them up. On by default.

retention.title: Retention policy
retention.desc: Retention is counted in local-date day-files, today included. These records belong to this device and are shared by every companion. An expired day-file is not deleted right away: it goes only once every enabled learning consumer of every companion (periodic learning, skill generation) has read that day. Only when every companion has both switched off does expired mean deleted.
retention.daysDesc: How many days raw events are kept at most ({{min}}–{{max}}).
retention.capacityDesc: A hard cap on the event directory ({{min}}–{{max}} MiB) that overrides retention: once usage exceeds it, the oldest day-files are deleted first, even if learning has not read them yet.
retention.empty: No collected event files are stored.
retention.lowerConfirm: Lowering retention or the storage limit runs a cleanup immediately, which may delete the oldest raw records and cannot be undone. These records are shared by every companion, so the cleanup affects all of them. Extracted memories and skills are kept. Continue?

stopAll.title: Stop everything
stopAll.desc: Turn off every collection source above and stop periodic learning and skill generation for every companion in one go.
stopAll.actionDesc: Switches only, no deletion: models and intervals stay as they are, learned skills and memories are kept, and already-collected raw records are still cleaned by the retention policy above. It stops learning for every companion, not just the one whose tab this is.
stopAll.confirm: Turn off every collection source and stop periodic learning and skill generation for every companion? You can re-enable at any time with no model reconfiguration. Already-collected raw records are not deleted.
stopAll.partial: Collection has stopped, but learning could not be stopped for some companions. Press again to retry — the ones already stopped are unaffected.
stopAll.failed: Could not turn things off. Please retry.

disclosure.title: Let your companion learn you
disclosure.body: Once on, your companion learns from how you use the platform (tool calls, tasks, chats) and distills skills and memories automatically. All data stays local — view, clear, or turn it all off anytime under Data Sources.
disclosure.enabled: Enabled — your companion will learn from your usage

evolve.title: Skill evolution
evolve.hint: Distills skills from your repeated multi-step actions, using the shared learning model above.
evolve.reflectHint: Also reflect after a complex task whether it's worth saving
evolve.autoActivateHint: Strongly-repeated high-confidence skills activate directly (still revocable in the Skills tab)
evolve.consolidateHint: Reviews existing skills daily and folds ones that do the same thing into one (the rest are archived, restorable in the Skills tab)

archive.title: Session archiving
archive.hint: Long companion chats grow the context ever larger and costlier. When enabled, an idle chat window is compressed into a day-partitioned diary and the live context is reset — keeping the companion lean and able to take on denser work.
archive.reviewEmpty: No archived session diaries yet. Once session archiving is on, idle chats settle here by day.
archive.onThisDayEmpty: No records from this day in past years yet.

collaboration.title: Smart collaboration
collaboration.hint: When enabled, the companion can split complex work across collaborators, make progress in parallel, and combine the results. Simple tasks are still handled directly.

remote.accessHint: Reach {{companionName}} from outside the desktop app: external MCP / REST clients connect as it with an access token.
remote.accessTokenGrant: Anyone holding this token acts as {{companionName}} on the remote API: reading and writing its memories, invoking its skills, starting conversations on its behalf, and anything else the remote API exposes — effectively full control of this companion. Treat it like a password and revoke it the moment it leaks.
remote.accessRegenerateConfirm: Regenerating invalidates the old token immediately and disconnects any external client still using it. Continue?
remote.accessRegenerateUnknownConfirm: We can't tell right now whether this companion already has an access token. If it does, generating a new one invalidates the old token immediately and disconnects any external client still using it. Continue?

evolution.learningDesc: This companion reviews your work records on the schedule below and files what it distills under its own name.
evolution.learnEnabledDesc: When off, periodic learning stops; memories and skills already distilled are left untouched.
evolution.modelDesc: The chat model used to review records and distill memories and skills.
evolution.modelMissing: No model selected — learning and skill generation won't run.
evolution.modelStale: The selected {{model}} is no longer in the available model list, so learning will fail — please pick another.

evolution.preferenceAggressiveDesc: High-confidence skills activate straight away; the rest stay drafts (you can disable any of them in the Skills tab).

evolution.quietRangeDesc: During this window the desktop companion stops popping bubbles at you and unread notices pile up on its badge; scheduled learning and skill generation are skipped until it wakes. Incoming messages are still answered. Leave it empty to allow interruptions all day.

history.dayLoadFailed: This day did not load — tap to retry
history.dayTruncatedHint: This day is long; showing only its earliest {{count}} messages.

other.migrateSectionDesc: Pack this companion up for another device, or restore a companion from a bundle.
other.exportDesc: Pack “{{companionName}}” into a .zip bundle and import it on another device to restore it. Its settings, growth progress, bound knowledge-base names and custom figure image are always in the bundle; memories and skills are up to you. Chat history is not included.
other.importDesc: Pick a companion bundle (.zip) to create a new companion here and rebind its knowledge bases by name.
other.dangerSectionDesc: Nothing here can be undone — confirm before you run it.
other.deleteHint: Permanently deletes “{{companionName}}” along with its memories, skills, growth progress and chat history.
other.deleteConfirmBody: “{{companionName}}”’s settings, every memory it holds under Memory, its skills, growth progress and chat history are all deleted permanently and cannot be recovered. The bundle above can carry its settings, memories and skills, but chat history is not in it, so exporting first will not keep that.

danger.deleteConfirmBody: This permanently deletes “{{companionName}}” together with all of its memories, skills, growth progress and chat history, and cannot be undone. Note: the migration bundle can carry settings, memories and skills, but chat history is not in it, so exporting first will not keep that.

robot.title: Robot connection
robot.hint: Attach a physical robot to {{companionName}}: it speaks with this companion's persona, models and memories.
robot.otaStep: 1. Open the robot's Wi-Fi setup page and set the OTA address under Advanced settings to one of these:
robot.otaNone: No LAN address is available yet.
robot.codeStep: 2. On boot the robot shows and reads out a 6-digit activation code. Enter it here:
robot.claimOk: The robot is now bound to {{companionName}}
robot.claimNotFound: No such activation code, or it has expired — check the number on the robot's screen again.
robot.claimTaken: This robot is already bound to another companion. Unbind it there first.
robot.lanOff: The robot needs LAN access turned on before it can reach this computer.
robot.lanEnableFailed: Failed to turn on LAN access
robot.lanUnavailable: Turn on LAN access from the desktop app.
robot.unbindConfirm: After unbinding, this robot belongs to no companion and shows an activation code again, waiting to be claimed.
robot.removeConfirm: Deleting revokes the device token immediately; the robot has to report in and be bound again.
robot.loadFailed: Could not read the robot list — check that the robot service is running.
